As the state's only veterinary teaching hospital, the Veterinary Medical Teaching Hospital (VMTH) at the Texas A&M College of Veterinary Medicine & Biomedical Sciences (VMBS) is a model of excellence in veterinary healthcare and education. We are committed to improving lives through exceptional veterinary education, large and small animal patient care, service, and discovery.

New World Screwworm: What You Need to Know
Many of you have seen recent headlines: New World Screwworm
(Cochliomyia hominivorax)
has arrived in Texas from Mexico. We’ve assembled information for those who work with various small animal groups about what they need to know and will continue to add more information as this situation develops.
New World Screwworm Information Hub
Small Animal Teaching Hospital (SATH)
For appointments and emergency care, call 979.845.2351.
The Small Animal Teaching Hospital (SATH) at the
College of Veterinary Medicine & Biomedical Sciences (VMBS)
is a premier companion animal hospital recognized for excellence in patient care. The SATH holds accreditation from the
American Animal Hospital Association
, Level I Emergency and Critical Care Facility certification from the
Veterinary Emergency + Critical Care Society
, and Gold-level Cat Friendly Practice® status.
Large Animal Teaching Hospital (LATH)
For appointments and emergency care, call 979.845.3541.
The Large Animal Teaching Hospital (LATH) at the
College of Veterinary Medicine & Biomedical Sciences (VMBS)
is a leading destination for large animal care, serving horses, cattle, and other hoofstock. The hospital offers a broad range of specialty and field services — ranging from dermatology to theriogenology — and is home to one of the few full-time farriers employed by a U.S. veterinary college.
Clark Small Animal Hospital
Our new, state-of-the-art small animal hospital, slated to open in 2027, will better serve the community and educate the next generation of Aggie veterinarians.

About Us
We are a teaching hospital within the College of Veterinary Medicine & Biomedical Sciences (VMBS) at Texas A&M University.
Clinical Trials
Clinical trials are approved by the VMBS’ Clinical Research Review Committee, ensuring our patients’ best interests are protected.
Telemedicine
Our telemedicine program offers visits with clinicians via live video interaction for clients and referring veterinarians.
Hospital Support
Meet the people behind the scenes — working in the laboratories, pharmacy, and administration — who make Texas A&M’s VMTH so special.
Outreach & Service
The VMTH is committed to helping underserved communities through outreach and service programs and initiatives.
Giving
Invest in the future of animal health by supporting our new hospital construction, specialty programs, compassionate care initiatives, or the VMTH’s greatest needs.
What Our Clients Say About Us
“I never expected so much compassion when it
comes to animal care. From the person at the
front desk to the assistant who checked us in
and the doctor who met with us, it was the
best possible care we could have received.”
Kaylin Scott
whose Sphynx, Kai, was treated by
the SATH Soft Tissue Surgery Service
“He’s thriving and gets to live as a normal
horse now, which blows my mind. I’m so
grateful to everybody at Texas A&M who
was part of his healing journey.”
Rachel Denton
whose quarter horse Rooster was
treated for a baseball-sized lump in
his neck by LATH surgeons
“(Participating in the ‘Better Breathing’ clinical
trial) is about making sure they can breathe and
move comfortably for as long as possible. They
still look like bulldogs; they just look like healthy
bulldogs.”
Felicia Beswick
owner of Jax and Tun, who lost
a combined 21 pounds in the trial
Patient Stories
The VMTH is home to 31 services, giving patients access to a full spectrum of veterinary care, from preventive medicine to minimally invasive procedures and other specialty services.
Patient Stories »
Veterinary Technology Education Partnership
Through a collaborative partnership, students in Blinn College District’s Veterinary Technology Program receive hands-on training in every aspect of the wide-ranging animal health field through acess to Texas A&M VMBS resources, faculty, and facilities. Blinn’s is the only community college veterinary technology program in Texas with the opportunity to complete laboratory and clinical experiences at the VMTH.
